item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Stockholm Peace Research Institute --Sweden官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Global aid gap widens as major donors prioritize higher military spending, new SIPRI research shows

发布源: Stockholm Peace Research Institute --Sweden | 抓取时间: 2026-10-31

(Stockholm, 27 October 2026) There is a widening gap between the official development assistance (ODA) provided by major donor countries and actual development and humanitarian needs, which could have potentially serious consequences for human security and political stability, according to a new report released today by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI). The gap could be closed with only a small fraction of the resources committed to new military spending.

SIPRI data show that global military spending last year reached US$2.9 trillion, the highest level ever recorded, equivalent to 2.5 per cent of global GDP. At the same time, ODA has been falling since 2024, based on figures from the Organization for Economic Development and Cooperation (OECD). The authors further show that core ODA provision started to stagnate in 2021 but this was temporarily obscured by a substantial increase in aid to Ukraine following Russia’s full-scale invasion and in ‘in-donor refugee costs’ (ODA by the donor to cover the costs of hosting refugees). The biggest decreases in core ODA spending have been on economic infrastructure and health.

‘Wealthy states in Europe and beyond have sharply increased their military spending in response to rising military threats. But this has coincided with deep cuts in other budget lines, including development and humanitarian aid. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在The Ratio Institute – SwedenThis link opens in a new window官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Article (with peer review)Artificial Intelligence and Management: The Automation-Augmentation ParadoxRaich, S. & Krakowski, S.

发布源: The Ratio Institute – SwedenThis link opens in a new window | 抓取时间: 2026-10-31

Taking three recent business books on artificial intelligence (AI) as a starting point, we explore the automation and augmentation concepts in the management domain. Whereas automation implies that machines take over a human task, augmentation means that humans collaborate closely with machines to perform a task. Taking a normative stance, the three books advise organizations to prioritize augmentation, which they relate to superior performance. Using a more comprehensive paradox perspective, we argue that, in the management domain, augmentation cannot be neatly separated from automation. These dual AI applications are interdependent across time and space, creating a paradoxical tension. Over-emphasizing either augmentation or automation fuels reinforcing cycles with negative organizational and societal outcomes. However, if organizations adopt a broader perspective comprising both automation and augmentation, they could deal with the tension and achieve complementarities that benefit business and society. Drawing on our insights, we conclude that management scholars need to be involved in research on the use of AI in organizations. We also argue that a substantial change is required in how AI research is currently conducted in order to develop meaningful theory and to provide practice with sound advice.

Raich, S. & Krakowski, S. (in press).Artificial Intelligence and Management: The Automation-Augmentation Paradox. Academy of Management Review.

Academy of Management Review

item.content:encoded:
Labour market research

发布源: The Ratio Institute – SwedenThis link opens in a new window | 抓取时间: 2026-10-31

One of Ratio’s three research areas is the labour market. Within this field, topics such as the future of work, challenges of the Swedish model, labour market regulations, skills supply and skills match are included.

The research is multidisciplinary. ProfessorLotta Sternis responsible for the research area at the institute.

Ratio is also a partner institute to theAI-Econ Lab, an international and multidisciplinary research team, with participants from eight countries and four disciplines (economics, computer science, management, statistics), led by the Ratio researcher Magnus Lodefalk among others.
